concepts.def: Northwest and west: older, harder rocks (granite, slate); higher relief; e.g. Scottish Highlands, Lake District, Snowdonia.
Southeast: younger, softer sedimentary rocks (chalk, clay); flatter relief; e.g. London Basin, East Anglia.
Diagonal line dividing UK between upland west/north and lowland south/east; reflects geological boundary.
Last Ice Age (until c.10,000 years ago) shaped uplands with U-shaped valleys, corries, ribbon lakes.
UK's 17,820km coast includes rocky (Cornwall), chalk (Dover), sandy (East Anglia), estuarine (Severn).
Major rivers (Thames, Severn, Trent) flow from uplands to lowlands; demonstrate upper, middle, lower course features.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The Changing Landscapes of the UK — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Changing Landscapes of the UK brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The Changing Landscapes of the UK.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which line divides upland and lowland Britain?
options: Watford Line
Tees-Exe Line
Hadrian's Wall
Severn-Trent Line

mcqs.q: Where are softer sedimentary rocks found in UK?
options: Scottish Highlands
Southeast England
Snowdonia
Lake District

mcqs.q: What changed between the MDGs (Millennium Development Goals) and the SDGs (Sustainable Development Goals)?
options: MDGs and SDGs are the same — just renamed.
Plates move because of ocean tides pulling on the crust.
The SDGs replaced the MDGs because the MDGs were achieved.
MDGs (2000-2015) targeted LICs on basic poverty/health/education; SDGs (2015-2030) apply to all countries and include environmental and inequality goals — broader, more universal scope.

mcqs.q: Why do people move from rural to urban areas in LICs?
options: Because cities in poor countries are always better than the countryside.
Because the government forces them to move to cities.
A combination of push factors (rural poverty, lack of services, agricultural change) and pull factors (perceived jobs, education, healthcare) — though reality often disappoints.
MDGs and SDGs are the same — just renamed.

mcqs.q: What drives the movement of tectonic plates?
options: Convection currents in the mantle combined with slab pull at subduction zones and ridge push at constructive boundaries.
Because the government forces them to move to cities.
Plates move because of ocean tides pulling on the crust.
The Earth's rotation makes the plates move.
